name: Redis Cluster
tagline: Shards keys across masters with replicas and automatic failover; serves sessions and cache.

howItWorks.title: Hash slots
howItWorks.body:
Slot = CRC16(key) mod 16384; each master owns a slot range.
A wrong node answers MOVED; clients cache the slot map.
Multi-key commands need one slot; force it with {hash tags}.
A hot tag creates a hot slot; use tags sparingly.

howItWorks.title: Masters and replicas
howItWorks.body:
Replication is asynchronous; a failover can lose the last writes.
Gossip runs on the cluster bus, client port plus 10000.
A node unanswered past cluster-node-timeout becomes PFAIL, then FAIL by majority.
The replica with the best offset wins the election and takes the slots.
Keep three masters so a majority survives one loss.

howItWorks.title: Client topology refresh
howItWorks.body:
Lettuce does not refresh the topology after failover by default.
Enable periodic refresh and all adaptive refresh triggers.
MOVED, ASK and persistent reconnects then reload the slot map.
Without it, the app errors until restart.

howItWorks.title: Memory and eviction
howItWorks.body:
maxmemory caps RAM; maxmemory-policy acts at the cap.
noeviction rejects writes; allkeys-lru evicts any key, volatile-lru only keys with a TTL.
Watch evicted_keys and used_memory against maxmemory.
Keep the host limit well above maxmemory for fork copy-on-write.

howItWorks.title: Persistence and sessions
howItWorks.body:
RDB forks and snapshots; fast restore, loses writes since the last dump.
AOF logs every write; everysec bounds loss to about one second.
A frontend session cache: TTL on every key, allkeys-lru or volatile-lru.
Pure cache loss is tolerable; session loss logs users out.

flow: Client hashes the key: CRC16 mod 16384 gives the slot.
The command goes to the master that owns the slot.
A wrong guess returns MOVED; the client updates its slot map.
The master writes to memory, appends to AOF, streams to replicas.
At maxmemory the eviction policy drops keys or rejects the write.
Peers mark an unresponsive master PFAIL, then FAIL by majority.
A replica wins the election and takes over the slots.
Lettuce adaptive refresh reloads the topology; traffic resumes.

deploy.summary: Six Redis 7.2.5 nodes on three Ubuntu 22.04 VMs: two ports each, systemd-managed, hardened.
prerequisites: Three Ubuntu 22.04 VMs on one subnet
A sudo user and your SSH public key
DNS or hosts entries for redis1..3
Repeat steps 1 to 5 on every VM

steps.title: SSH key login and sshd hardening
steps.code:
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C ops@workstation
ssh-copy-id ops@10.0.0.11
ssh ops@10.0.0.11 'sudo tee /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-harden.conf' <<'EOF'
PasswordAuthentication no
PermitRootLogin no
KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
AllowUsers ops
EOF
ssh ops@10.0.0.11 'sudo sshd -t && sudo systemctl reload ssh'
steps.note: Test a second session before closing the first. 10.0.0.x is a placeholder.

steps.title: Static address
steps.code:
sudo tee /etc/netplan/60-static.yaml <<'EOF'
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    ens18:
      dhcp4: false
      addresses: [10.0.0.11/24]
      routes:
        - to: default
          via: 10.0.0.1
      nameservers:
        addresses: [10.0.0.2]
EOF
sudo chmod 600 /etc/netplan/60-static.yaml
sudo netplan apply
steps.note: Placeholders: interface, addresses, DNS. Add A records redis1..3.lab.local on your DNS server.

steps.title: Firewall
steps.code:
sudo ufw allow from 10.0.0.0/24 to any port 22 proto tcp
sudo ufw allow from 10.0.0.0/24 to any port 7000:7001 proto tcp
sudo ufw allow from 10.0.0.0/24 to any port 17000:17001 proto tcp
sudo ufw --force enable
steps.note: 17000:17001 is the cluster bus (port plus 10000). Subnet is a placeholder.

steps.title: Build Redis
steps.code:
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential curl
curl -fsSLO https://download.redis.io/releases/redis-7.2.5.tar.gz
tar xzf redis-7.2.5.tar.gz
make -C redis-7.2.5 -j2
sudo make -C redis-7.2.5 install
sudo useradd --system --home /var/lib/redis --shell /usr/sbin/nologin redis

steps.title: Config and systemd unit
steps.code:
sudo mkdir -p /etc/redis && sudo tee /etc/redis/template.conf <<'EOF'
bind NODEIP
port PORT
protected-mode yes
dir /var/lib/redis/PORT
cluster-enabled yes
cluster-config-file nodes.conf
cluster-node-timeout 5000
appendonly yes
appendfsync everysec
maxmemory 512mb
maxmemory-policy volatile-lru
requirepass CHANGE_ME
masterauth CHANGE_ME
EOF
for p in 7000 7001; do
  sudo install -d -o redis -g redis /var/lib/redis/$p
  sed "s/PORT/$p/g; s/NODEIP/10.0.0.11/" /etc/redis/template.conf | sudo tee /etc/redis/$p.conf >/dev/null
done
sudo chown redis: /etc/redis/*.conf && sudo chmod 640 /etc/redis/*.conf
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/redis@.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Redis %i
After=network-online.target
[Service]
User=redis
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/redis-server /etc/redis/%i.conf
LimitNOFILE=65535
Restart=on-failure
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now redis@7000 redis@7001
steps.note: Replace CHANGE_ME and NODEIP per VM. Use volatile-lru for sessions with TTLs.

steps.title: Create the cluster
steps.note: Run once, from any VM. redis-cli keeps each replica off its master's host where it can.

steps.title: Test failover
steps.code:
redis-cli -h 10.0.0.12 -p 7000 cluster nodes | grep master
ssh ops@10.0.0.11 sudo systemctl stop redis@7000
sleep 8
redis-cli -h 10.0.0.12 -p 7000 cluster nodes
ssh ops@10.0.0.11 sudo systemctl start redis@7000
steps.note: The replica of the stopped master is promoted; the old master returns as a replica.

steps.title: Lettuce topology refresh
steps.code:
spring:
  data:
    redis:
      password: ${REDIS_PASSWORD}
      cluster:
        nodes: redis1.lab.local:7000,redis2.lab.local:7000,redis3.lab.local:7000
        max-redirects: 3
      lettuce:
        cluster:
          refresh:
            adaptive: true
            period: 30s
steps.note: Spring Boot 3.x property names. Boot 2.x uses spring.redis.

verify: redis-cli -p 7000 cluster info | grep cluster_state   # ok
redis-cli -p 7000 cluster keyslot 'user:{42}:cart'   # equals the :profile key
pitfalls: Cluster bus port (client plus 10000) blocked by a firewall splits the cluster.
Lettuce without adaptive refresh keeps hitting the dead master after failover.
Multi-key commands across slots fail with CROSSSLOT.
maxmemory equal to host RAM invites the OOM killer during fork.
noeviction on a cache turns memory pressure into application errors.
Asynchronous replication drops recent writes on failover; Redis is not the source of truth.
KEYS and huge values block the single event loop; use SCAN.
keyPoints: CRC16(key) mod 16384 maps every key to one hash slot.
Each master owns slots; replicas promote when a majority marks it FAIL.
maxmemory plus an eviction policy decides what happens at the cap.
Lettuce adaptive refresh moves clients to the new master without a restart.
quickDeploy: Harden SSH and set static addresses
Build Redis 7.2.5 and run it under systemd
Create the cluster with one replica per master
Stop a master and watch the failover
osiNote: RESP over TCP; the cluster bus gossips on client port plus 10000.
production: Size maxmemory at 60% of RAM; leave room for fork and buffers.
Place each replica on a different host than its master.
Persist with AOF everysec; run RDB snapshots from a replica.
Require ACL users and a firewall limited to the cluster subnet.
Alert on evicted_keys, used_memory ratio and cluster_state not ok.
